from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Introduction: The Restricted Puzzle", 
            [
                'Meet the standard Towers of Hanoi puzzle.', 
                'But here, disks only move to adjacent pegs.', 
                'Jumping from A to C is strictly forbidden.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_PEG = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_DISK1 = "#3357FF" # Small
        COLOR_DISK2 = "#33FF57" # Medium
        COLOR_DISK3 = "#FF5733" # Large
        COLOR_ARROW = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_FORBIDDEN = "#FF0000"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create Pegs
        peg_a = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["E2"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        peg_b = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["E4"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        peg_c = Line(self.grid["B6"], self.grid["E6"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PEG)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PEG)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PEG)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "F6")

        # Create Disks (Initial state on Peg A)
        # disk3 is bottom, disk1 is top
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.4, height=0.4, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=COLOR_DISK3, stroke_width=0)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.0, height=0.4, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=COLOR_DISK2, stroke_width=0)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.6, height=0.4, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=COLOR_DISK1, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(disk3, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C2")

        self.play(
            FadeIn(peg_a), FadeIn(peg_b), FadeIn(peg_c),
            FadeIn(label_a), FadeIn(label_b), FadeIn(label_c),
            FadeIn(disk3), FadeIn(disk2), FadeIn(disk1)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Double arrows between pegs to indicate adjacency restriction
        arrow_ab = DoubleArrow(self.grid["E2"] + RIGHT*0.7, self.grid["E4"] + LEFT*0.7, color=COLOR_ARROW, stroke_width=4, tip_length=0.2)
        arrow_bc = DoubleArrow(self.grid["E4"] + RIGHT*0.7, self.grid["E6"] + LEFT*0.7, color=COLOR_ARROW, stroke_width=4, tip_length=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_ab), Create(arrow_bc))
        
        # Animate the smallest disk sliding from Peg A to Peg B, then from Peg B to Peg C
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), run_time=1)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C6"]), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Draw a red cross over a dashed curved arrow between Peg A and Peg C
        jump_arrow_base = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B2"] + UP*0.4, self.grid["B6"] + UP*0.4, angle=-PI/2, color=COLOR_FORBIDDEN)
        jump_arrow = DashedVMobject(jump_arrow_base, num_dashes=20)
        
        cross_line1 = Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT, color=COLOR_FORBIDDEN, stroke_width=10).scale(0.5)
        cross_line2 = Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT, color=COLOR_FORBIDDEN, stroke_width=10).scale(0.5)
        red_cross = VGroup(cross_line1, cross_line2)
        self.place_in_area(red_cross, "A3", "B5") 
        
        self.play(Create(jump_arrow), FadeIn(red_cross))
        
        # Flash the three disks on Peg C and highlight the start (A) and end (C) pegs
        # Snap other disks to C to show target state
        self.play(
            disk3.animate.move_to(self.grid["E6"]),
            disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"]),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.play(Flash(self.grid["D6"], color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, flash_radius=1.2))
        
        rect_a = SurroundingRectangle(label_a, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        rect_c = SurroundingRectangle(label_c, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect_a), Create(rect_c))
        
        self.wait(2)

            [
                'Counting usually happens in binary or decimal.', 
                'Ternary uses digits zero, one, and two.',

                'Each digit represents a peg: A, B, or C.',

            ]

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        dec_label = Text("Decimal: 0-9", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")

        self.place_at_grid(bin_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        
        tern_label = Text("Ternary: 0, 1, 2", font_size=32, color="#87CEEB")
        self.place_in_area(tern_label, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(tern_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Odometer box
        box = Rectangle(height=1.2, width=3.0, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(box, "D2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Odometer digits
        d1 = Text("0", font_size=40)
        d2 = Text("0", font_size=40)
        d3 = Text("0", font_size=40)
        digits = VGroup(d1, d2, d3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        digits.move_to(box.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(box), FadeIn(digits))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Incrementing 000 -> 001
        new_d3_1 = Text("1", font_size=40).move_to(d3)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(d3, new_d3_1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Incrementing 001 -> 002
        new_d3_2 = Text("2", font_size=40).move_to(new_d3_1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(new_d3_1, new_d3_2))
        self.wait(0.5)

            ReplacementTransform(new_d3_2, new_d3_0)

            Text("1 = Peg B", font_size=20, color="#87CEEB"),
            Text("2 = Peg C", font_size=20, color="#90EE90")

        # Color existing digits based on mapping
        self.play(

            new_d2_1.animate.set_color("#87CEEB"),
            new_d3_0.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            FadeIn(peg_legend)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFC0CB"))
        
        # 111 in ternary = 13 in decimal

        final_d1 = Text("1", font_size=40, color="#87CEEB").move_to(d1)
        final_d2 = Text("1", font_size=40, color="#87CEEB").move_to(new_d2_1)
        final_d3 = Text("1", font_size=40, color="#87CEEB").move_to(new_d3_0)

            ReplacementTransform(new_d2_1, final_d2),
            ReplacementTransform(new_d3_0, final_d3)
        )
        
        calc_text = Text("(1 x 9) + (1 x 3) + (1 x 1) = 13", font_size=24, color="#FFC0CB")
        self.place_in_area(calc_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(calc_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Every disk configuration has a unique ternary address.",
            "Largest disks are the most significant digits.",
            "Smallest disks represent the least significant digits.",
            "State 'zero-two' means big on A, small on C.",
            "Three disks create twenty-seven unique state addresses."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mapping States to Ternary Coordinates", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for highlighting
        COLOR_1 = YELLOW
        COLOR_2 = BLUE_B
        COLOR_3 = GREEN_B
        COLOR_4 = ORANGE
        COLOR_5 = PINK

        # Common Mobjects: Pegs
        peg_width = 0.1
        peg_height = 2.5
        pegs = VGroup(
            Rectangle(width=peg_width, height=peg_height, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY),
            Rectangle(width=peg_width, height=peg_height, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY),
            Rectangle(width=peg_width, height=peg_height, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.2)
        
        peg_labels = VGroup(
            Text("A (0)", font_size=18),
            Text("B (1)", font_size=18),
            Text("C (2)", font_size=18)
        )
        for i, label in enumerate(peg_labels):
            label.next_to(pegs[i], DOWN, buff=0.2)

        pegs_and_labels = VGroup(pegs, peg_labels)
        self.place_in_area(pegs_and_labels, "C1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Disks
        disk_large = Rectangle(width=1.4, height=0.3, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_2)
        disk_small = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.3, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_3)

        # Function to position disks on pegs
        def get_disk_pos(disk, peg_index, height_index):
            base_pos = pegs[peg_index].get_bottom()
            return base_pos + UP * (0.3 * height_index + 0.15)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_1))
        self.play(Create(pegs), Write(peg_labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2))
        disk_large.move_to(get_disk_pos(disk_large, 0, 0))
        addr_text_l2 = Text("Digit 1 (MSB)", font_size=24, color=COLOR_2)
        self.place_at_grid(addr_text_l2, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_large), FadeIn(addr_text_l2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3))
        disk_small.move_to(get_disk_pos(disk_small, 0, 1))
        addr_text_l3 = Text("Digit 2 (LSB)", font_size=24, color=COLOR_3)
        self.place_at_grid(addr_text_l3, "A5")
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_small), FadeIn(addr_text_l3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_4))
        
        # State '02': Large on A (0), Small on C (2)
        new_disk_large_pos = get_disk_pos(disk_large, 0, 0)
        new_disk_small_pos = get_disk_pos(disk_small, 2, 0)
        
        address_display = Text("Address: 0 2", font_size=36)
        address_display[8].set_color(COLOR_2) # 0
        address_display[9].set_color(COLOR_3) # 2
        self.place_at_grid(address_display, "B4")

        self.play(
            disk_large.animate.move_to(new_disk_large_pos),
            disk_small.animate.move_to(new_disk_small_pos),
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(addr_text_l2, addr_text_l3), address_display)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_5))
        
        # Clear specific config to show grid
        self.play(FadeOut(pegs_and_labels), FadeOut(disk_large), FadeOut(disk_small), FadeOut(address_display))
        
        # Create a 3x3 grid of states
        states_3x3 = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            row_group = VGroup()
            for j in range(3):
                state_label = Text(f"{i}{j}", font_size=24, color=COLOR_5)
                row_group.add(state_label)
            row_group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
            states_3x3.add(row_group)
        states_3x3.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        grid_title = Text("All 9 States (N=2)", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        total_3x3 = VGroup(grid_title, states_3x3).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(total_3x3, "B2", "E5")
        
        n3_info = Text("For N=3: 3^3 = 27 states", font_size=20, color=COLOR_5)
        self.place_at_grid(n3_info, "F4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(total_3x3))
        self.play(Write(n3_info))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            'Valid moves connect states into a geometric graph.',
            'The restricted rule creates a linear state path.',
            'One disk forms a simple three-node line.',
            'Two disks form three lines in a triangle.',
            'Three disks generate the intricate Sierpinski Gasket fractal.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of Moves: The Sierpinski Gasket", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for each stage
        colors = ["#88C0D0", "#A3BE8C", "#EBCB8B", "#D08770", "#BF616A"]

        # Helper to generate Sierpinski Graph nodes recursively
        def get_gasket_points(order, center, side_length):
            if order == 0:
                return [center]
            
            # Distance from center to vertices of a triangle
            h = side_length * np.sqrt(3) / 6
            # Sub-centers for recursive triangles
            # Top, Bottom-Left, Bottom-Right
            c1 = center + np.array([0, h, 0])
            c2 = center + np.array([-side_length / 4, -h / 2, 0])
            c3 = center + np.array([side_length / 4, -h / 2, 0])
            
            if order == 1:
                return [c1, c2, c3]
            
            points = []
            points.extend(get_gasket_points(order - 1, c1, side_length / 2))
            points.extend(get_gasket_points(order - 1, c2, side_length / 2))
            points.extend(get_gasket_points(order - 1, c3, side_length / 2))
            return points

        # Helper to build the visual graph
        def build_graph(points, color, node_radius=0.08):
            nodes = VGroup(*[Dot(p, radius=node_radius, color=WHITE) for p in points])
            edges = VGroup()
            n = len(points)
            
            # Simple heuristic for Sierpinski edges: connect points in groups of 3
            # plus the connections between the sub-triangles
            def connect_recursive(idx_start, count):
                if count == 3:
                    # Base triangle edges
                    e1 = Line(points[idx_start], points[idx_start+1], stroke_width=2, color=color)
                    e2 = Line(points[idx_start+1], points[idx_start+2], stroke_width=2, color=color)
                    e3 = Line(points[idx_start+2], points[idx_start], stroke_width=2, color=color)
                    edges.add(e1, e2, e3)
                    return
                
                sub_count = count // 3
                connect_recursive(idx_start, sub_count)
                connect_recursive(idx_start + sub_count, sub_count)
                connect_recursive(idx_start + 2 * sub_count, sub_count)
                
                # Connect the sub-triangles at their adjacent vertices
                # (Specific to standard Sierpinski numbering: top corner of sub2 to bottom corner of sub1 etc)
                # For simplicity in this animation, we draw lines based on proximity
                pass

            if n == 3:
                edges.add(Line(points[0], points[1], color=color), 
                          Line(points[1], points[2], color=color), 
                          Line(points[2], points[0], color=color))
            elif n > 3:
                # Add edges for within sub-triangles and link them
                for i in range(0, n, 3):
                    edges.add(Line(points[i], points[i+1], color=color, stroke_width=2))
                    edges.add(Line(points[i+1], points[i+2], color=color, stroke_width=2))
                    edges.add(Line(points[i+2], points[i], color=color, stroke_width=2))
                
                # Add connections between triangles for n=9 and n=27

                if n == 9:
                    # Connect the three blocks of 3
                    edges.add(Line(points[2], points[3], color=color))
                    edges.add(Line(points[5], points[6], color=color))
                    edges.add(Line(points[8], points[0], color=color))
                elif n == 27:
                    # Sub-connections for 9s
                    for j in range(0, 27, 9):
                        edges.add(Line(points[j+2], points[j+3], color=color))
                        edges.add(Line(points[j+5], points[j+6], color=color))
                        edges.add(Line(points[j+8], points[j+0], color=color))
                    # Major connections for 27s
                    edges.add(Line(points[8], points[9], color=color))
                    edges.add(Line(points[17], points[18], color=color))
                    edges.add(Line(points[26], points[0], color=color))

            return VGroup(edges, nodes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing layout
        lecture_lines = [
            "Solving means traversing the fractal's outer perimeter.",
            "We move from state 'zero-zero-zero' to 'two-two-two'.",
            "This path visits every single vertex on the edge."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Graph Traversal: Finding the Optimal Path", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Recursively build Sierpinski Gasket Depth 3
        def get_gasket_lines(depth, p1, p2, p3):
            if depth == 0:
                return [Line(p1, p2), Line(p2, p3), Line(p3, p1)]
            m12 = (p1 + p2) / 2
            m23 = (p2 + p3) / 2
            m31 = (p3 + p1) / 2
            return (get_gasket_lines(depth - 1, p1, m12, m31) +
                    get_gasket_lines(depth - 1, m12, p2, m23) +
                    get_gasket_lines(depth - 1, m31, m23, p3))

        # Initial relative positions for a large triangle
        rel_top = np.array([0, 2.5, 0])
        rel_bl = np.array([-2.5, -2.0, 0])
        rel_br = np.array([2.5, -2.0, 0])
        
        gasket_lines_raw = get_gasket_lines(3, rel_top, rel_bl, rel_br)
        gasket = VGroup(*gasket_lines_raw).set_stroke(color="#ADD8E6", width=1.5)
        
        # Position Gasket in the designated 6x6 grid area
        self.place_in_area(gasket, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Extract the positioned vertices for the perimeter path
        # Bounding box corners of the depth-3 gasket correspond to the 000, 111, 222 states
        g_top = gasket.get_top()
        g_left = gasket.get_corner(DL)
        g_right = gasket.get_corner(DR)
        
        # Constrained path: 000 (Top) -> 111 (Bottom Left) -> 222 (Bottom Right)
        # Side length is 2^3 = 8 steps. Total path nodes = 9 + 8 = 17.
        path_points = []
        for i in range(9):
            path_points.append(interpolate(g_top, g_left, i / 8))
        for i in range(1, 9):
            path_points.append(interpolate(g_left, g_right, i / 8))
        
        self.play(Create(gasket), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        
        label_000 = Text("000", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_222 = Text("222", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # Position labels near the corners
        label_000.next_to(g_top, UP, buff=0.15)
        label_222.next_to(g_right, DOWN, buff=0.15)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label_000), FadeIn(label_222))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold color matching path
        
        moving_dot = Dot(color="#FFD700").scale(1.2)
        moving_dot.move_to(path_points[0])
        
        traced_path = VGroup()
        
        # Start with a flash at the first node
        self.add(moving_dot)
        self.play(Flash(path_points[0], color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.25), run_time=0.3)
        
        # Trace path segment by segment and flash each node
        for i in range(len(path_points) - 1):
            p_start = path_points[i]
            p_end = path_points[i+1]
            
            segment = Line(p_start, p_end, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4)
            segment_glow = segment.copy().set_stroke(width=10, opacity=0.3)
            
            self.play(
                moving_dot.animate.move_to(p_end),
                Create(segment),
                FadeIn(segment_glow),
                run_time=0.2,
                rate_func=linear
            )
            traced_path.add(segment, segment_glow)
            
            # Flash at each vertex reached
            self.play(Flash(p_end, color=YELLOW, flash_radius=0.2, line_length=0.1), run_time=0.1)

        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        TITLE_COLOR = "#FFD700"  # Golden glowing
        L1_COLOR = "#A0DFFF"     # Light blue
        L2_COLOR = "#D4FFD4"     # Light green
        L3_COLOR = "#FFD4FF"     # Light magenta
        
        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion: The Beauty of Mathematical Convergence", 
            [
                "Ternary logic and fractals reveal the same truth.", 
                "Simple rules build infinite, self-similar geometric patterns.", 
                "The constrained puzzle unifies counting, graphs, and geometry."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(L1_COLOR)
        
        # Helper to generate Sierpinski triangle vertices and edges
        def get_sierpinski_points(order, center, side_length):
            height = (3**0.5 / 2) * side_length
            top = center + UP * (height / 2)
            left = center + LEFT * (side_length / 2) + DOWN * (height / 2)
            right = center + RIGHT * (side_length / 2) + DOWN * (height / 2)
            
            if order == 0:
                return [top]
            
            new_side = side_length / 2
            h_offset = height / 4
            w_offset = side_length / 4
            
            pts_top = get_sierpinski_points(order - 1, center + UP * h_offset, new_side)
            pts_left = get_sierpinski_points(order - 1, center + DOWN * h_offset + LEFT * w_offset, new_side)
            pts_right = get_sierpinski_points(order - 1, center + DOWN * h_offset + RIGHT * w_offset, new_side)
            
            return pts_top + pts_left + pts_right

        # Generate N=2 gasket vertices and labels (9 states)
        def get_ternary_label(index, order):
            res = ""
            for _ in range(order):
                res = str(index % 3) + res
                index //= 3
            return res

        gasket_center = self.grid["D4"]
        n2_points = get_sierpinski_points(2, gasket_center, 4.0)
        
        # Create visual nodes and labels
        nodes = VGroup()
        labels = VGroup()
        for i, pt in enumerate(n2_points):
            dot = Dot(pt, radius=0.08, color=L1_COLOR)
            lbl = Text(get_ternary_label(i, 2), font_size=14, color=WHITE).next_to(dot, UP, buff=0.1)
            nodes.add(dot)
            labels.add(lbl)

        # Create basic triangle outline for N=2
        # For simplicity in logic, we draw the 3 main large triangles
        edges = VGroup()
        def create_triangle_lines(p1, p2, p3):
            return VGroup(Line(p1, p2, stroke_width=2), Line(p2, p3, stroke_width=2), Line(p3, p1, stroke_width=2))

        # Hardcoded triangles for N=2 visually
        h = (3**0.5 / 2) * 4.0
        p_top = gasket_center + UP * (h / 2)
        p_left = gasket_center + LEFT * 2 + DOWN * (h / 2)
        p_right = gasket_center + RIGHT * 2 + DOWN * (h / 2)
        p_mid_tl = (p_top + p_left) / 2
        p_mid_tr = (p_top + p_right) / 2
        p_mid_b = (p_left + p_right) / 2
        
        edges.add(create_triangle_lines(p_top, p_mid_tl, p_mid_tr))
        edges.add(create_triangle_lines(p_left, p_mid_tl, p_mid_b))
        edges.add(create_triangle_lines(p_right, p_mid_tr, p_mid_b))
        edges.set_color(L1_COLOR).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)

        self.play(Create(edges), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes), Write(labels), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(L2_COLOR)

        # Recursive function to generate lines for higher-order Gasket
        def get_gasket_lines(order, center, side):
            if order == 1:
                h = (3**0.5 / 2) * side
                t = center + UP * (h / 2)
                l = center + LEFT * (side / 2) + DOWN * (h / 2)
                r = center + RIGHT * (side / 2) + DOWN * (h / 2)
                return VGroup(Line(t, l), Line(l, r), Line(r, t))
            
            new_side = side / 2
            h = (3**0.5 / 2) * side
            h_off = h / 4
            w_off = side / 4
            
            g1 = get_gasket_lines(order - 1, center + UP * h_off, new_side)
            g2 = get_gasket_lines(order - 1, center + DOWN * h_off + LEFT * w_off, new_side)
            g3 = get_gasket_lines(order - 1, center + DOWN * h_off + RIGHT * w_off, new_side)
            return VGroup(g1, g2, g3)

        # Build N=6 Gasket
        n6_gasket = get_gasket_lines(6, gasket_center, 4.0)
        n6_gasket.set_stroke(width=1, color=L2_COLOR)

        # Hide L1 elements and "zoom out" by scaling down N=2 and replacing with N=6
        self.play(
            FadeOut(labels),
            FadeOut(nodes),
            FadeOut(edges),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Show growth of fractal complexity
        self.play(FadeIn(n6_gasket), run_time=1)
        
        # Simulating zoom out: scale the gasket and the camera effectively
        # Note: We scale down the gasket to show it getting "smaller" or "further"
        self.play(
            n6_gasket.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(self.grid["D4"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(L3_COLOR)

        # Glowing Final Title
        final_title = Text("The Fractal Path: Ternary Logic", font_size=36, color=TITLE_COLOR)
        # Position at center of visual area
        self.place_in_area(final_title, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Make it "glow" with a shadow/duplicate or just a bold appearance
        glow = final_title.copy().set_stroke(TITLE_COLOR, width=8, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(
            n6_gasket.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2),
            Write(final_title),
            FadeIn(glow),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Fractal Path: Ternary Logic and the Constrained Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science/Mathematics) or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: The Restricted Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce the standard Towers of Hanoi but add a 'linear' constraint: disks can only move between adjacent pegs (A ↔ B and B ↔ C). A jump from A to C is forbidden. This restriction transforms a simple puzzle into a complex journey.
sections.example: A curious robot named 'Tertio' is trying to move 3 disks from Peg A to Peg C, but its mechanical arm is stuck—it can only shift disks to the peg immediately to its left or right.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Base-3 (Ternary) Counting
sections.content: Explain ternary counting (Base-3) where digits are 0, 1, and 2. Use a visual 'odometer' representation to show how numbers increment. Emphasize that while binary (Base-2) represents a 'yes/no' state, ternary represents 'left/middle/right' positions.
sections.example: Visualizing the number 13 in ternary: 111 (1*9 + 1*3 + 1*1). In our puzzle, each digit represents the peg location (0=A, 1=B, 2=C) of a specific disk.

sections.title: Mapping States to Ternary Coordinates
sections.content: Assign every possible configuration of the puzzle to a ternary number. For N disks, there are 3^N possible states. The largest disk is the most significant digit, and the smallest disk is the least significant digit.
sections.example: With 2 disks, state '02' means the large disk is on Peg A (0) and the small disk is on Peg C (2). This creates a unique 'address' for every possible layout of the game.

sections.title: The Geometry of Moves: The Sierpinski Gasket
sections.content: Visualize the state space as a graph. Each valid move between states is an edge. Because of the linear constraint, the state-transition graph forms a perfect Sierpinski Triangle (fractal). Moving one disk corresponds to moving along an edge of the triangle.
sections.example: An animation shows that for 1 disk, the graph is a line (A-B-C). For 2 disks, it becomes three connected lines forming a triangle. For 3 disks, it becomes the classic Sierpinski Gasket with 27 vertices.

sections.title: Graph Traversal: Finding the Optimal Path
sections.content: Explain that solving the puzzle is equivalent to traversing the 'outer edge' of the Sierpinski triangle. To get from state 000 (all on Peg A) to 222 (all on Peg C), the robot must visit every single node on the perimeter of the fractal.
sections.example: Trace a glowing line following the perimeter of the Sierpinski triangle. The sequence of nodes visited matches the sequence of ternary numbers if we follow a 'Gray Code' style path for the constrained puzzle.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Mathematical Convergence
sections.content: Summarize how ternary counting (number theory), the Towers of Hanoi (algorithms), and the Sierpinski Triangle (fractal geometry) are actually three different ways of looking at the same underlying structure.
sections.example: Zoom out from the small 3-disk triangle to a massive 10-disk Sierpinski fractal, showing how the robot's simple rules create a complex, infinite geometric pattern.
